flashcard_questions.q: What is clock speed in a processor?
flashcard_questions.a: The number of cycles the CPU carries out each second.

flashcard_questions.q: Which unit is clock speed measured in?
How many clock cycles per second does one gigahertz mean?

flashcard_questions.a: Running a CPU faster than its factory clock speed to gain performance.

flashcard_questions.q: Why do overclocked computers need effective cooling such as fans?
What is a cache hit in a processor?
flashcard_questions.a: When the CPU finds the data it needs already stored in the cache.

flashcard_questions.q: What happens when the CPU cannot find the data it needs in the cache?
flashcard_questions.a: A cache miss occurs, so the data must be fetched from slower RAM.

flashcard_questions.q: Why does a larger cache improve CPU performance?
flashcard_questions.a: It holds more data, so more requests become cache hits instead of slow RAM trips.

flashcard_questions.q: Which level of cache is the smallest and fastest?
Which level of cache is the largest and slowest of the three?
What is a core inside a CPU?
flashcard_questions.a: A complete processing unit that can run the fetch-execute cycle on its own.

flashcard_questions.q: What is parallel processing on a multi-core CPU?
flashcard_questions.a: Several cores working on different instructions at the same time.

flashcard_questions.q: Why does doubling the number of cores rarely double real-world performance?
flashcard_questions.a: Some tasks are sequential, so their steps cannot be shared between cores.

flashcard_questions.q: What number of cores does a quad-core processor have?
